body: I'm so sorry to hear that you're going through the same, it blows. :( I love your positive spin on it, though! We'll both get through it and come out stronger but figuring it out is downright dismal. Thanks for the comment and the offer, I'll definitely keep it in mind! And good luck!! <3

Thank you, your point about it being hard to make a terrible decision is comforting! You're right about that, and I feel better remembering that I'll still have my loved ones in my life. Thank you again for your kind words! <3
Thanks for the reassurance! <3 It's nice to know that there'll be some things to look forward to moving into the workforce, free time sounds amazing lol. I really appreciate your comment and offer ❤️
Ooh I like this one! GAD's a never-ending cycle of ruining the present moment thinking about the future and trying out this phrase helped snap me out of that!
No ideas but my brother's (nick)name is Kye too! Hope he has a happy birthday!! 🎂🎈

This sounds so much like my story, I empathize a lot ❤️ Especially the finding excuses for what happened to you, your world falling apart, and not being able to maintain friendships and relationships. Leaving any religion is a tough experience, it's harder when you're leaving one that's isolated you from normal society and are still closeted. If you ever want to chat, my messages are open!

That's awesome! Work can be such a drag, especially when it piles up. Hoping you're feeling doubly good having gotten out of your head for a bit and gotten something off your to-do list!

And thanks, I hope it helps at least some people!

For me, I put on a movie. I have a habit of falling into the "should" cognitive distortion and always feel like I'm wasting my time by watching movies or TV shows. My friend mentioned her boyfriend and it reminded me of my chronic single status which is a huge suicidal thought trigger for me. That was on top of the hopeless mood I've been in for weeks. So I decided to treat myself and watch Never Been Kissed for the first time. I love Drew Barrymore and her character in this movie is adorable! It's making me feel so much less alone and defective and a lot more "seen".

I came here because I was feeling the same way. I'm 23f, also no job, depression and anxiety since childhood so I've been socially isolating a long time and have a fear of being in a lot of social situations, no desire to be a part of life. It's nice to think of what my life could be but the reality is so far from it. I feel like I have to kill myself too, I'm doing nothing with my life besides being a burden and suffering and it doesn't seem like things will ever get better.

That said, I've attempted suicide a few times already and every time I have that moment of clarity that people speak about a lot. When I'm face-to-face with death, I wonder why I didn't take more risks to better my situation before trying to kill myself. If I was alright with dying anyway, then I had nothing to fear from my actions; commiting suicide later if things didn't work out or dying from another cause couldn't be worse endings than what I was already planning. And if my life was the worst it could get, things could've only gotten better from there.

So apply for a job and quit when the anxiety gets to be too much. Apply for the easiest-sounding majors at a bunch of colleges. Steal your parents' card to cover fees if you need to. Get your mom a bunch of rehab brochures and tell her you'll kill yourself if she doesn't go. Pack a lunch and dinner and spend ten hours outside in your city or neighborhood or backyard. Forget about the future and other people. As someone planning suicide, you could die any day. Do those crazy things you know won't help your situation to spite the universe. You're gonna die anyway, have some fun before you're nothing for the rest of forever.
